songs.title: FIVE : THIRTY
songs.verdict: A tight three-minute house cut from a Beirut project, small on paper but one that keeps getting played here.
songs.body:
THE MASKING TAPES is a Beirut-based electronic project working in minimal house and tech house, usually in longer tracks. “FIVE : THIRTY” is a self-released house single (3:07) from January 2025, with no label or producer credits attached.

**Hook**, **Groove**, **Build & drop** and **Sound design:** nothing published describes the track, so the details have to come from the listen. What's documented is the lane: stripped-back, minimal-leaning house from a scene with few outlets, at radio-edit length rather than a long DJ tool.

Replay is the strongest evidence: 47 plays in the owner's library, the most of anything in this batch. The knock is exposure, not quality: no press, no bio and a short runtime that may leave DJs wanting an extended mix.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (47 plays): 6.8K Spotify monthly listeners; self-released (℗ 2025 THE MASKING TAPES), no label. Lane: Beirut minimal/tech house. Sources: Spotify track/artist pages; Apple album https://music.apple.com/us/album/five-thirty-single/1788871213 (genre House); Bandcamp https://themaskingtapes.bandcamp.com/album/the-masking-tapes-vol-1 (Beirut, tags). Doubts: the Bandcamp page doesn't list FIVE : THIRTY. I matched it to the same act through the name and the track MARI, which appears both on Bandcamp and as an Apple single. No bio, producer credit or social links foun

songs.title: U.
songs.verdict: A tech-house club tool from a US deep-tech DJ and an Argentine minimal producer that keeps earning repeat plays.
songs.body:
ChaseWest is a US house DJ/producer whom EDM Identity tagged a rising deep-tech talent with a strong catalog of edits; Discip, from Neuquén, Argentina, makes minimal and tech house with hip-hop influences and has released on Revival New York, Desolat and Take Notes. "U." is one of two tracks on their Dopamine EP (Revival New York, July 2023), produced by both.

**Groove:** this lane lives or dies on the groove, and it's made for long DJ blends. **Sound design** and **Build & drop** are the parts to check on the listen; no write-up describes the track itself.

It's a dancefloor tool rather than a song, and 16 plays in Marku's library say it holds up outside the club. The limit: without a home-listening hook, it may stay a mix staple rather than a standout.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (16 plays): ChaseWest has 90,973 Spotify monthly listeners; Discip's count wasn't found because his Spotify page failed to load. Original Mix - Song by ChaseWest & Discip') and album https://music.apple.com/us/album/dopamine-single/1695609152; YouTube Topic video (credits Discip and ChaseWest as producers); Insomniac pages for both artists. songs.title: Maybe the Problem Is Me
songs.verdict: An early, self-released bedroom-pop single from a South London voice who has since become one of the city's names to watch.
songs.body:
dexter in the newsagent is Charmaine Ayoku, a South London alt-R&B and bedroom-pop artist now on Dork's Hype List and opening for Blood Orange and Jim Legxacy. “Maybe the Problem Is Me” is a self-released single from January 2021, before her first EP.

**Lyrics:** the title points at self-blame; no write-up covers the song, so check the details after listening. **Vocals & delivery:** FADER now calls her a soulful storyteller, and this is an early look at that voice. **Production:** a 2021 independent bedroom-pop release, so expect it rougher than her recent work.

This sits in the owner's library with 11 plays, which says it holds up past the novelty of an early single. The knock: it is a sketch next to her newer mixtape material, and almost no one has written about it.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (11 plays): her main Spotify profile has 108.9K monthly listeners. The single sits on a separate older profile (https://open.spotify.com/artist/1ey2ESMWC5HEj2CmxvD7Mp, 2.6K). Chartmetric says 131.4K. Label: the single is ℗ 2021 independent; Wikipedia lists AWAL / Common Knowledge / Rules the World and a self-released 2025 mixtape. No major deal found. Lane: South London alt-R&B / bedroom pop. Sources: Wikipedia, Dork Hype List 2026, Spotify album https://open.spotify.com/album/0SsPfnh3JLRz8mKRjKD4BB, Apple album https://music.apple.com/us/album/maybe-the-proble

songs.title: Makeup
songs.verdict: Quiet, introspective Riverside R&B that leaves room for a warm voice and the feelings behind it.
songs.body:
Brandon is a Riverside, California singer-songwriter with Trinidadian roots who taught himself writing and production and names Sam Cooke, Stevie Wonder and Smokey Robinson as touchstones. He wrote “Makeup” in October 2018 during a burst of writing, put it out as a single in 2019, and it later landed on his debut EP Coming Clean.

**Vocals & delivery:** press calls his voice warm and soulful, and that’s the center of his sound. **Production:** the Coming Clean material is sparse and calm, recorded between a college dorm and his bedroom. **Lyrics:** the EP deals with a hard year, gentle words to past lovers and learning to forgive himself. Okayplayer singled out “Makeup” as a highlight for its intimacy.

Fifteen plays in the owner’s library says it holds up. The knock: the low-key, minimal approach rarely raises its voice, so it can drift past anyone not leaning in.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (15 plays): 63.3K Spotify monthly listeners; self-released (℗ 2023 Brandon), no label named. Lane: Inland Empire introspective R&B. Sources: Ones to Watch Q&A (Riverside; Makeup written Oct 2018; minimal production), Okayplayer feature, Apple single https://music.apple.com/br/album/makeup-single/1702648645?l=en-GB, Apple album Coming Clean https://music.apple.com/br/album/coming-clean/1719882754?l=en-GB, Spotify Coming Clean album (Makeup is track 2). Doubts: the Spotify link is the album, not the track; Marku's library says 2019 album but the single is 2019 an

songs.title: Six Million
songs.verdict: Lo-fi house from a German Bandcamp project that sits between beat tape and dancefloor, made for background rotation.
songs.body:
upper class is a German lo-fi project with a large Bandcamp catalogue, tagged lofi house, lofi hip hop and house. “Six Million” comes from the 2018 release Haus Vibes for House Wives, and Apple files it under House.

**Hook**, **Groove**, **Build & drop** and **Sound design:** no write-ups or credits exist, so the specifics are for the listen. The lane is clear: house rhythm with lo-fi hip-hop texture, built for mood rather than peak-time impact.

With 87K monthly Spotify listeners, the project has found its audience, and the owner has come back to this one 10 times. The knock: lo-fi house is a crowded, interchangeable lane, and nothing documented sets this track apart from the rest of the catalogue.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (10 plays): 87.1K Spotify monthly listeners; self-released on Bandcamp, no label found. Lane: German lo-fi house / lofi hip-hop. Sources: Bandcamp track page (Germany, tags, IG instagram.com/upperclasslofi, SoundCloud soundcloud.com/upperclasslofi), Spotify track/artist, Apple song, Deezer track. Doubts: release date differs by store (Bandcamp/Apple 13 Mar 2018, Spotify/Deezer 28 Jun 2018). No bio or credits; the Bandcamp 'about' text just says 'placeholder'. Older release, added from Marku's library (freshness rule waived).

songs.title: It's Not Serious

Mike Kota is a US indie-pop and indie-rock artist with a long run of self-released singles and projects, including Turning a Corner, Through Fire and Rift, and around 19K monthly Spotify listeners. "It's Not Serious" came out as a single on Nov 11, 2022, filed under Alternative.

No press, credits or sound description exist for this song, so the parts (**Melody & hook**, **Vocals**, **Production**, **Lyrics**) are for the listener to fill in.

It's on the radar because Marku follows him and has it in his library. Until the listen, it sits mid-scale: steady output, little outside signal.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's follows (@mike_kota) and his Apple Music library: 19,207 Spotify monthly listeners; no label found. Lane: US indie pop/rock. Sources: Spotify track/artist pages (IG instagram.com/mike_kota, X @mike_kota_), Shazam single page https://www.shazam.com/album/1774384602/its-not-serious-single (where the Apple link came from), Dork track page, Viberate. Older release, added from Marku's library (freshness rule waived).

songs.title: Can I
songs.verdict: A low-tempo alt-rap single from a tiny US act, co-produced in a small crew and released with zero fanfare.
songs.body:
BABYKIRA is a very small US alternative hip-hop artist who drops singles often and turns up on other people's projects. “Can I” came out Nov 28, 2025 on the label broke.

**Production:** BABYKIRA co-produced it with Noah Mejia, Dylan Morris and Arham Paul, who also share the writing, and Kevin Miranda mixed it. Shazam lists it at 87 BPM, so it sits in a laid-back pocket. **Vocals & delivery** and **Lyrics:** nothing has been written about either; describe them after listening.

It is in the owner's library and follows, which counts for something. The knock: no press, no bio and no Spotify presence, so this one rests entirely on the listen.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's follows (@babykira) and his Apple Music library: Spotify listeners unknown (Viberate N/A; Deezer shows 36 fans), so clearly underground. Label 'broke' per Shazam, not a major. Lane: US alt hip-hop (Apple keyword: Alternative). Sources: Shazam song page https://www.shazam.com/en-us/song/1854615810/can-i, Apple artist page, Deezer artist page, Viberate. Doubts: very little public bio (no city, no producer credits); no Spotify link or Instagram found. Older release, added from Marku's library (freshness rule waived).

songs.title: FKA Passat
songs.verdict: A 1:28 mood fragment from Alex Banin’s Since Winona: brief enough to loop, too short to fully land.
songs.body:
Alex Banin is a London-born, New York-raised singer who started making music in Chicago, blending R&B with pop melodies and citing Amy Winehouse, Frank Ocean and Lauryn Hill. She self-releases, and her 2023 single “Doc Whiler” passed 9 million Spotify plays. “FKA Passat” is track 4 on the seven-song Since Winona.

**Structure:** at 1:28 it plays like an interlude, a passing scene rather than a full verse-chorus song. **Lyrics:** she calls herself an introspective writer who mostly writes about relationships, but no source covers this track’s words. **Production:** no credits are listed.

Seventeen plays in the owner’s library is a strong sign it works in context. The limit: as a standalone it’s a fragment, and how much it hits depends on hearing it inside the album.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (17 plays): Spotify shows 150,474 monthly listeners and 23.5K followers. Apple album copyright is ℗ 2024 Alex Banin (self-released, no label), so keep. Instagram alxbanin and website sincewinona.com are both listed on the Spotify artist page. Sources: Spotify track, album and artist pages; Apple song and album (https://music.apple.com/us/album/since-winona/1744112397). Doubts: no city or bio found. A Max's Music Mondays Substack interview exists but is paywalled. Listener count is just over 100k. Older release, added from Marku's library (freshness rule waived)

songs.title: Girls
songs.verdict: A 130 BPM indie-tech roller on Revival New York, built for DJs and lean enough to land on Beatport's minimal/deep charts.
songs.body:
Dan Molinari is a US house DJ, producer and vocalist whose sound Insomniac calls raw; his breakout was the D.O.P.E. EP and he often works with SLAMM. “Girls” (Original Mix) came out Jan 17, 2025 on Revival New York: 5:26 long, 130 BPM, in E minor, filed as indie tech.

**Groove** is the point: the length and tempo mark it as a DJ tool built to mix. **Hook**, **Build & drop** and **Sound design:** no write-up describes them, so check on the listen whether his own vocal features. It turned up in a Beatport chart of 2025's best minimal/deep tracks so far.

The owner has played it 19 times, a solid sign it holds up outside a set. The knock: club-tool structure means a long runway, and away from a dancefloor it may feel like it's waiting for the next track.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (19 plays): about 64.9K Spotify monthly listeners, independent dance label Revival New York (Apple shows ℗ 2025 Revival New York), so keep. Lane: house / indie tech. Sources: Apple single page, Beatport https://www.beatport.com/track/girls/19969524, the Insomniac artist page (also the source of the Instagram handle), and the Spotify track and artist pages. Doubts: Insomniac doesn't say which city he's based in. Older release, added from Marku's library (freshness rule waived).

songs.title: Ion Cake
songs.verdict: Detroit's Kura brings his fast, auto-tuned runs to a Ghostrage beat on the opener of their six-song tape.
songs.body:
Kura is a Detroit rapper-producer who started making music at 14, signed with Pi'erre Bourne's SossHouse at 17, and landed "jjjound" on The Fader's top rap songs of 2024. "Ion Cake" opens 6 Songs, a short tape released through Ghostrage LLC in November 2024, with Ghostrage producing and engineering.

**Vocals & delivery:** Kura's calling card is elastic, melody-first flows that flip between staccato and quick auto-tuned runs. **Production:** Ghostrage handles the whole tape, so the beat choice is the variable. **Lyrics:** playful bragging is his usual mode.

Eight plays in Marku's library point to real replay. The limit: a one-producer side tape tends to be a sketchbook next to a main release, and the listen should check whether it stands on its own.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (8 plays): Kura has about 50K Spotify monthly listeners and Ghostrage about 16.6K. Shazam lists the label as Ghostrage LLC, so keep. Lane: Detroit melodic trap. Shazam credits Ghostrage as producer/engineer and Daniel McAllister and Chandler Ingram as writers. Sources: Apple song, Shazam (https://www.shazam.com/en-us/song/1771893634/ion-cake), Spotify track, Audiomack (https://audiomack.com/kura/album/ion-cake), and Wikipedia's Kura (musician) page. songs.title: Feito Fumaça (feat. Ju Strassacapa)
songs.verdict: A Brazilian trio's nostalgic love song where a lost love hangs around like smoke in a closed room.
songs.body:
Obinrin Trio are Lana Lopes, Elis Menezes and Raíssa Lopes, a feminist trio formed after Carnaval 2016 who write original songs on traditional Brazilian rhythms like maracatu, côco, jongo and baião. “Feito Fumaça” is track 5 on their self-released album Origem (Apr 2020), with a guest vocal from Ju Strassacapa.

**Lyrics:** written by Raíssa Lopes, it is about memory and longing, with the past love pictured as smoke filling a closed room. **Vocals & delivery:** all three members sing, and the guest adds a fourth voice. **Production:** the band's lineup is acoustic guitar, percussion and drums; which rhythm drives this track isn't documented.

The owner has 11 plays on it, a good sign for a song in Portuguese with almost no press. The knock: a quiet folk record about longing won't grab anyone looking for energy.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (11 plays): about 11.9K Spotify monthly listeners. Shazam lists the label as 'Obinrin Trio [distributed by Tratore]', so self-released. Keep. Sources: Apple song page, Shazam, the Spotify track and artist pages, and Catraca Livre's feature on the trio. Doubts: Spotify now credits the guest as LAZÚLI instead of Ju Strassacapa. songs.title: Navy Blue
songs.verdict: A short, self-released R&B single that has kept its place in the owner’s rotation with little fanfare.
songs.body:
HASANI is a self-releasing R&B/soul artist, with songwriting credited to Wayne (W. Hasani) Miller. “Navy Blue” was a standalone single on Nov 8, 2016, and runs 2:43. His later catalog includes singles like “All U Need” and “Steady” and the album Make No Promises.

**Production:** no producer credit is public, and there’s no press on the track. **Structure:** under three minutes, it’s a compact single rather than a showcase.

Sixteen plays in the owner’s library is the strongest evidence here and points to a song that rewards return visits. The limit: there’s almost nothing public about it, so this draft rests on the listen.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (16 plays): about 27.3K Spotify monthly listeners. Shazam lists the label as 'Hasani' (self-released). Keep. Sources: Apple song page, Shazam (https://www.shazam.com/song/1275216660/navy-blue), and the Spotify track and artist pages. Doubts: almost no public bio, city or press. The verdict and body are deliberately thin. Older release, added from Marku's library (freshness rule waived).

songs.title: ZIG ZAGGING
songs.verdict: A two-minute alt-R&B glide: sweet vocal, sleek bass, gated guitar plucks, and a darker double meaning underneath.
songs.body:
Asha Imuno is an LA alt-R&B and rap artist who calls himself a multihyphenate. “ZIG ZAGGING” (2:04) built buzz as a TikTok snippet before its May 2022 release, on his own WAITINGROOM imprint.

**Melody & hook:** Dusty Organ hears an infectious, groove-led track. **Vocals & delivery:** smooth and sweet, with flows the site calls syrupy. **Production:** a steady drum loop, sleek bass and gated guitar plucks that trail the vocal. **Lyrics:** a double reading, either hopeful about dreams coming true or paranoid about staying unpredictable to dodge danger.

At two minutes it's over before it outstays anything, which explains the owner's 12 plays. The knock: the brevity cuts both ways, and with no credited producer or follow-through, it plays more like a strong sketch than a full statement.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (12 plays): about 97K Spotify monthly listeners, close to the 100k line. Apple shows '℗ 2022 WAITINGROOM', which appears to be his own imprint or concept; no major found. Keep. Sources: dustyorgan.com/2022/06/02/asha-imuno-shares-blissful-new-single-zig-zagging/, the Apple single page (UA storefront), the Spotify track (fetched with tracking params, which I stripped from the ID URL) and artist page, and onestowatch.com. Doubts: no producer named, and no official Instagram found. Older release, added from Marku's library (freshness rule waived).

songs.title: K-Hole
songs.verdict: A 1:25 sketch from Juto's Fleece EP, short enough to loop and apparently good enough to keep looping.
songs.body:
Juto is an LA-based singer-songwriter raised in Gwinnett, Georgia, the first signing to Taco Bennett's RE7AX Records, whose R&B and pop draws on the gospel he grew up with. He plays six instruments and once opened for Lauryn Hill. "K-Hole" is track 4 of the seven-song, 18-minute Fleece EP (Dec 2021), written by him alone.

**Melody & hook:** at 1:25, it's interlude length, so any hook has to land fast. **Vocals & delivery:** his voice is the main instrument on a cut this short. **Production** and **Lyrics** aren't documented beyond his sole writing credit.

22 plays in Marku's library is a strong signal for something this brief. The obvious knock: it's a sketch, and it may feel unfinished to anyone not already in his world.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (22 plays): about 28.7K Spotify monthly listeners. Qobuz lists the label as COR - TAN; Wikipedia says RE7AX Records in association with COR/TAN. Both are indie, so keep. Sources: Apple song page, Spotify track and artist pages, Qobuz (https://www.qobuz.com/gb-en/album/fleece-juto/e8xji271ktz5b; credits Jairus Gay as writer, no producer listed), and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juto. Doubts: release date is Dec 17 on Apple but Dec 21 on Spotify/Qobuz. Wikipedia spells his name 'Jarius'. Older release, added from Marku's library (freshness rule waived).

d4mon. is an underground R&B/soul artist, about 35K monthly listeners, who moves with UoT, SupremeDae and LOM MAZI. 2S!des came out May 16, 2025 (℗ Moyne): 8 songs in about 24 minutes.

At 24 minutes, it is short enough to replay whole, and it is in the owner's library and follows. The knock: no press and almost no public bio, so there is little outside proof that it reaches past his own circle.

songs.title: NEW CHANEL (feat. d4mon. & LOM MAZI)
songs.verdict: A three-minute, three-voice posse cut from a Jersey singer-rapper who moves easily between bars and melody.
songs.body:
SupremeDae is a singer and rapper from Somerset, New Jersey, who grew up writing raps with his uncle in front of MTV Jams and names Drake, Kanye West and Lil Wayne as influences. Reviews have called his lyrics raw and his melodies distinctive. “NEW CHANEL” is a 3:04 single from April 2025 with d4mon. and LOM MAZI, a trio that also teamed up on “Flawed.”

**Vocals & delivery:** his calling card is switching between singing and rapping. **Production:** no credits are public. **Lyrics:** no write-up covers this track’s subject, so the read rests on his lane: candid, diary-style writing.

Posse cuts live or die on chemistry, and these three keep coming back to each other. The limit: with no coverage or credits, the draft can’t say much past the lane, and a later four-way version adds confusion.

songs.title: a-list
songs.verdict: One piece of a 25-track, world-building DIY album from an LA producer who treats his records as soundtracks.
songs.body:

**Production:** he builds mostly with Ableton's stock tools and runs guitar through a Chroma Console pedal, and calls his music cinematic, a soundtrack. **Melody & hook**, **Vocals** and **Lyrics:** nothing published covers this track, so the details are for the listen.

The owner has played it 9 times, a fair signal for an artist this small. The knock: on a 25-track concept album, a single song can depend on context, and it has had almost no outside coverage.

songs.title: All The Rage
songs.verdict: A Vancouver rock collective stitches new wave and cowboy grunge into something of its own on a self-produced single.
songs.body:
Hotel Decor is a Vancouver collaborative rock project that calls its music an ever-evolving collage, from '70s new wave to cowboy grunge, built from the eras it loves. "All The Rage" (March 2021) was written and produced by Csaba Laszlo, mixed and mastered by Roberto Angel Dwyer, and released on indie label Mammal Sounds Records, with a video by DualSense Films.

**Production:** a single writer-producer keeps the vision tight. **Melody & hook**, **Vocals** and **Lyrics** aren't described in any source, so the listen will have to fill those in.

Ten plays in Marku's library say it sticks. The knock to check: genre collage can land as reference-spotting unless the song itself is strong enough to hold the pieces together.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (10 plays): Spotify shows about 27.5K monthly listeners on indie Mammal Sounds Records. Vancouver rock. songs.title: Keep Your Head Up
songs.verdict: A calm, self-produced acoustic pep talk that found a life of its own on Reels.
songs.body:
Khi Infinite is a Virginia Beach artist working between R&B, hip-hop and bedroom pop, with a Pusha T and CHASE B credit on “LIGHTS PLEASE”. “Keep Your Head Up” was his first release of 2022, an acoustic track he produced himself.

**Production:** a calm, restrained instrumental that leaves room for the voice. **Vocals & delivery:** warm and sincere, per the write-ups. **Lyrics:** about self-trust and growth from the inside; he has said progress starts within, and the title works as plain encouragement. **Melody & hook:** described as uplifting, and the sound passed three million views on Instagram Reels.

The owner has 13 plays on it, and the Reels run backs that up. The knock: an acoustic pep talk can feel slight, and it asks for a mood more than it demands attention.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (13 plays): Spotify shows about 57K monthly listeners. Label not found, but he's under the listener line so he qualifies either way. songs.title: Shit
songs.verdict: A 1:47 lo-fi punk blast about a lopsided relationship, from Philly DIY band Disaster Artist.
songs.body:
Disaster Artist are a Philadelphia DIY act tagged experimental, punk, rock and lo-fi on Bandcamp, where their bio is still a placeholder. “SHIT” is track 4 of 13 on the October 2022 album STOMACH PAINS and runs 1:47.

**Lyrics:** the posted lyrics deal with feeling neglected by a partner who’s pulling away toward someone else, and holding onto some pride anyway. **Production:** the lo-fi tag and self-release suggest a rough, unpolished recording. No credits are listed. **Structure:** under two minutes, it gets in and out.

Short and blunt songs like this tend to work in bursts. The knock: with no press and only tags to go on, the draft can’t judge the playing yet.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's follows (@disasterartistband) and his Apple Music library: Spotify shows about 4.3K monthly listeners, no label. Philly DIY punk. Sources: disasterartistband.bandcamp.com/album/stomach-pains (Oct 15, 2022; tracklist; Philadelphia; the band bio is just 'placeholder'); Spotify album page STOMACH PAINS (Oct 15, 2022).
